sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. April 14, 2025 announcement launches full GPT-4.1, mini and nano, describes capabilities and a nominal one-million-token context, and contains no nominal total or activated parameter count. No named base-model lineage with an established count is supplied.

sources.title: GPT-4.1 model
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 in official HTML and full documentation Markdown. Exact gpt-4.1 alias targets gpt-4.1-2025-04-14; current specification supplies context, modalities and supported features but no nominal total or active parameter count. The HTML retains the deprecated lifecycle designation. Context and capability values are not model-size measurements.

sources.title: GPT-4.1 Prompting Guide
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. April 14, 2025 prompting guide by OpenAI authors describes GPT-4.1 training, non-reasoning behavior, agentic tasks and exact-snapshot function calls. It supplies no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Full Markdown retrieved. Includes an exact gpt-4.1 request using document.pdf as input_file. Explains that PDF ingestion extracts text and page images and supplies both to the model; PDF is an API document format rather than a distinct native sensory modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: Full Markdown retrieved. October 14, 2026 notice lists GPT-4.1 snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 for shutdown January 14, 2027. Deprecated means scheduled retirement, distinct from completed shutdown. This notice does not change the original release date.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: August 5, 2025 release states gpt-oss were the first open-weight language models since GPT-2. Corroborates the earlier GPT-4.1 release was hosted rather than open weights. Architecture and counts disclosed for gpt-oss are not transferred to GPT-4.1. Initial direct fetch timed out; indexed full article text was subsequently accessible.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement applies to API access; sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited service access and reserve service intellectual property. Used for the descriptive Proprietary classification, not as a checkpoint license or a claim that these January 2026 terms governed the April 2025 launch.

sources.title: Training agents to self-report misbehavior
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. March 21, 2026 first-party research explicitly fine-tunes GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini separately through public APIs. Neither the post nor its linked full paper supplies a total or active parameter count; this fine-tune lineage does not identify a counted base model.

sources.title: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior
sources.publisher: Bruce W. Lee, Yueh-Han Chen and Tomek Korbak
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched October 27, 2026 at 15:42 UTC in /tmp/openai-parameter-primary-cache/07.source; all 5,563 extracted text lines searched and the GPT-4.1 training and evaluation sections read. Section 3.1 identifies GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini as separately fine-tuned API models. Parameter matches describe tool schemas and experiment settings, not model sizes. No nominal total, active count or counted-base lineage was found.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched October 27, 2026 at 15:42 UTC in /tmp/openai-parameter-primary-cache/08.source; all 3,105 extracted text lines searched and exact GPT-4.1 mentions inspected. Full-size GPT-4.1 appears in April 2025 health-model release chronology; a separate successor table concerns GPT-4.1-nano. Neither establishes full GPT-4.1 total or active parameters.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. February 18, 2026 guide by Erika Kettleson (OpenAI) describes Transformer-layer key/value caching and explicitly includes gpt-4.1; the archived guide covers models before GPT-5.6. It supplies no nominal total or activated count, and does not justify treating this model as dense or equating total with active.

sources.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
sources.evidence: Reopened original model-team report October 27, 2026. Section 4.1.1 explicitly identifies GPT-4.1 as an API baseline; Table 3 reports its benchmark scores without parameter counts. Tables 2 and 4 provide explicit total/activated rows for other named models, but do not include GPT-4.1. Those values cannot be transferred to this comparator.

sources.title: Identifying Fine-grained Forms of Populism in Political Discourse: A Case Study on Donald Trump’s Presidential Campaigns
sources.publisher: Ilias Chalkidis, Stephanie Brandl and Paris Aslanidis / EACL 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh original 18-page proceedings PDF inspected October 27, 2026. Section 3.1 identifies GPT-4.1 version 04/2025. Table 3 (PDF page 4) explicitly defines model size as total parameters and lists GPT 4.1 as n/a; no active count is supplied. This is an original empirical comparison, not an OpenAI disclosure; n/a here is an unavailable table value, not evidence that model parameters are inapplicable.

sources.title: Assessing French Readability for Adults with Low Literacy: A Global and Local Perspective
sources.evidence: Fresh original 23-page proceedings PDF inspected October 27, 2026. Appendix B.3 (PDF page 18) identifies GPT-4.1 with its exact official model-documentation link and states its parameter count is not publicly disclosed. The adjacent DeepSeek total/active figures belong to DeepSeek-R1, not GPT-4.1. This corroborates the absence of a reported count in the comparison, rather than constituting a developer specification.

sources.title: GPT-5 system card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 original PDF cache read in the re-audit. Later GPT-4.1 comparisons and safety evaluations supply no total or active parameter count for GPT-4.1; benchmark performance and family references are not size disclosures.

name.note: Exact full-size model, distinct from GPT-4.1 mini and nano.

developer.note: Official OpenAI release and hosted-model documentation identify the developer.

family.note: The original release and guide explicitly name the GPT-4.1 model family; use this specific family rather than generic GPT.

release_date.note: The dated announcement explicitly launches public API access that day. Later ChatGPT availability and the October 2026 deprecation are separate lifecycle events.

open_weights.note: Released through the hosted API. First-party open-weight release history corroborates that this GPT-4.1 release did not distribute weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the closed hosted model, not a named downloadable-checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: October 27 fresh re-audit found no supported nominal total in the exact OpenAI launch/specification, prompting/caching guides, later first-party fine-tuning research or full GPT-5 card. Targeted later original-research searches also found no count: Kimi K2 reports GPT-4.1 scores without size, EACL 2026 explicitly lists its total as unavailable, and EMNLP 2025 calls the count undisclosed. No explicit lineage to a counted base model was found. The null reflects missing nominal evidence, not a demand for an exact tensor census; unsubstantiated web estimates and sibling counts are excluded.

active_parameters_b.note: October 27 fresh re-audit separately searched active/activated-parameter terms and later original comparison tables. OpenAI sources provide no GPT-4.1 active count. Kimi K2 has explicit total/activated rows only for other models; its GPT-4.1 comparison gives scores, while the EACL and EMNLP papers supply no GPT-4.1 active figure. No supported nominal active convention or counted-base lineage was found. Transformer caching does not establish dense routing or active-equals-total.

architecture.note: Broad Transformer classification follows the documented inference mechanism and its explicit application to gpt-4.1, whose current alias targets gpt-4.1-2025-04-14. This is operational evidence, not a dedicated architecture report: it establishes a Transformer attention stack, but not a complete block inventory, exclusively Transformer layers, dense versus MoE feed-forward routing, or parameter counts. No sibling architecture is transferred.

context_window.note: The exact official specification is 1,047,576 tokens. The launch uses rounded 1M language. Retain the precise documented value; do not substitute 1,048,576 or confuse the separate 32,768 output cap with context.

modalities.note: Native model inputs are text and image, with text output. Keep PDF under the existing catalog convention for supported document input: the exact GPT-4.1 API example accepts a PDF and preprocesses it into text plus page images. No native PDF, audio or video sensory module is inferred.

reasoning.note: Both sources explicitly classify GPT-4.1 as non-reasoning. Prompted visible planning remains possible, but is distinct from a dedicated internal reasoning mode; false is supported directly rather than inferred from silence.

tool_call.note: Official model specification lists function calling and the exact dated snapshot is demonstrated producing function calls in the primary prompting guide.

description.value: Model for text and image understanding, coding, instruction following and long-context tasks.
description.note: Replace the unsubstantiated long-lived workhorse framing with documented inputs and tasks; omit current-best claims and unsupported size or architecture assertions.

sources.label: Identifying Fine-grained Forms of Populism in Political Discourse: A Case Study on Donald Trump’s Presidential Campaigns
Assessing French Readability for Adults with Low Literacy: A Global and Local Perspective

patch.notes: The gpt-4.1 alias defaults to gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, released in the API on April 14, 2025. Exact documented context is 1,047,576 tokens. PDF input is processed into text and page images. GPT-4.1 has no dedicated internal reasoning mode, but supports prompted visible planning and function calling. Transformer attention is documented; dense/MoE routing and nominal total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed after the October 27, 2026 source recheck. Deprecated October 14, 2026; API shutdown is scheduled for January 14, 2027, not already completed at review time.

summary: Parameter re-audit on October 27, 2026 preserves both counts as undisclosed after reopening exact OpenAI documentation, fresh full original papers and later original comparison tables. No supported nominal total, active-count convention or counted-base lineage was found; absence of an exact tensor census is not the reason for the nulls. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
